cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: test coverage sits at 31%, there is no coverage gate in continuous integration, and production systems of comparable complexity typically run 40-60% coverage.
cases.output: Test coverage sits at 31%, with no coverage gate in continuous integration. Systems of comparable complexity typically run 40 to 60% coverage in production. Without a gate, a regression can reach production unchallenged.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: deployments are performed manually by one engineer via SSH, there is no rollback procedure, and the last rollback attempt (8 months ago) took over 3 hours to complete.
cases.output: The most recent rollback attempt, 8 months ago, took over 3 hours to complete, and deployments are otherwise performed manually by a single engineer via SSH with no documented rollback procedure. This creates a single point of failure where service restoration depends entirely on one person's availability and manual execution. A regression reaching production would require that engineer to execute an unfamiliar and time-consuming procedure under pressure, with no tested path to recovery.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: one engineer holds sole access to the production database credentials, there is no documented access-handover process, and that engineer is on a rolling month-to-month contract.
cases.output: Production database credentials are held by a single engineer with no documented access-handover procedure. That engineer works on a month-to-month contract, creating a scenario where credential access could be lost on 30 days' notice with no defined transition path. There is no compensating control. Loss of access would halt all database administration until credentials could be rotated, and rotation itself requires the departing engineer's cooperation.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: customer personal data is retained indefinitely with no deletion policy, and there is no documented process for handling a data-subject deletion request.
cases.output: Customer personal data is retained indefinitely with no documented deletion policy. The company has no process for handling data-subject access or deletion requests, leaving it unable to comply with Article 17 of the GDPR or equivalent provisions in other jurisdictions. This is a critical gap with no compensating control. Remediation requires a data inventory, a retention schedule by data category, and a documented workflow for fulfilling deletion requests within the statutory timeframe.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) covering ALL of these facts: test coverage is 31%, there is no CI coverage gate, the last three production incidents were caused by untested edge cases, deployments are manual, and there is no rollback procedure. Do not omit any fact.
cases.output: Test coverage sits at 31%, with no coverage gate in continuous integration. The last 3 production incidents were caused by untested edge cases. Deployments are manual with no documented rollback procedure, meaning a regression can propagate to customers unchallenged and cannot be quickly reversed.

cases.input: Write three separate due-diligence findings, one paragraph each, clearly separated by a blank line. Finding 1 facts: passwords are stored in plaintext in the users table. Finding 2 facts: deployments are manual with no rollback procedure. Finding 3 facts: code comment style is inconsistent across the codebase, with no linting rule enforcing a convention.
cases.output:
Passwords are stored in plaintext within the users table, with no hashing or salting applied. Customer credentials are therefore exposed to any person with database access, and a breach of database credentials puts all user accounts at immediate risk of compromise. There is no compensating control. We recommend implementing industry-standard password hashing with a salt unique to each user, and rotating all existing passwords immediately upon deployment.

Deployments are performed manually via SSH by individual engineers with no documented procedure and no rollback capability. The most recent production issue, 3 weeks ago, required 45 minutes to resolve because there was no safe way to revert the change. Manual deployment is a single point of failure: if the engineer who typically deploys is unavailable, the company cannot release a fix. We recommend implementing automated deployment tooling with a tested rollback procedure exercised monthly.

Comment formatting varies widely across the codebase, with no linting rule to enforce a convention. Some files use block comments for functions while others use inline comments; some use sentence case and some use lowercase. This creates friction during code review and makes the codebase harder to navigate for new engineers. We recommend adopting a single comment style guide, implementing it as an automated lint check, and running the linter as a blocking gate in continuous integration.
